newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chronopost says 1996 traffic will show double-digit growth.
newsitem.headline: Chronopost says 1996 traffic will show double-digit growth.

text.p: French courier operator, Chronopost, said it was forecasting double-digit growth in its volume of traffic last year on 1995 levels.
1996 sales were estimated to total 2.096 billion francs compared to 2.089 billion francs, a Chronopost official told Reuters.
"Our provisional figures for 1996 show an average daily volume of 98,000 items compared to 87,000 items in 1995," a Chronopost official told Reuters.
The official said these estimates reflected the consolidation of Chronopost's position, in a growing express distribution market.
Domestic traffic accounts for around two-thirds of global volume while the remaining one-third is generated by international business.
Chronopost had a 16 percent share of France's domestic express market and 22 percent of its international traffic, the official added
Last month, Chronopost opened a new branch office at Macon, north of Lyon taking its network of French branches to 34.
The company planned to open a further four to five French branch offices in 1997 but their location would not be disclosed at this stage, the official said.
Chronopost is 66 percent-owned by the French post office and 34 percent by French aviation group, TAT SA. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
